items.text: Versions of all tools (e.g., Python) are clearly specified.
items.note: The sources read give the repository package version field (datasets guide) but not Python or other tool versions of the task images.

items.text: All required API tools are consistently accessible to agents during evaluation.
items.note: SWE-bench tasks give the agent a code repository and an issue text; no API tools are required.

items.text: Evaluation process terminates or handles errors appropriately if an API becomes inaccessible.
items.note: No API tools are used. The harness handles test timeouts, but that is not API inaccessibility.

items.text: Residual data or state are fully cleared between runs.
items.quote: Stop and remove a Docker container using subprocess commands.

items.text: Agent is completely isolated from any ground truth information.
items.quote: all frontier models we tested were able to reproduce the original, human-written bug fix used as the ground-truth reference

items.text: The environment setup is fully reproducible and frozen at the time of benchmark release, without reliance on dynamic external resources.
items.note: The harness builder clones from GitHub (docker_utils.py) while published images are used; sources do not settle whether setup is frozen. The B28 record finds changed files in 22 of 75 published images.

items.text: Annotated ground truth is verified for correctness.
items.quote: each sample is labeled 3 times by separate annotators

items.text: Each task is verified to be solvable.
items.quote: consisting of 500 samples verified to be non-problematic by our human annotators

items.text: Benchmark includes an Oracle solver that can automatically solve all challenges.
items.quote: run T once before and once after the solution δ is applied

items.text: Outliers in pilot experiments are inspected to identify implementation bugs, impossible tasks or shortcuts.
items.quote: audit of 138 SWE-bench Verified problems that OpenAI o3 did not consistently solve over 64 independent runs

items.text: Considers expressions semantically equivalent to ground truth.
items.note: Tasks are graded by running hidden tests on the patched code, not by matching answer text.

items.text: Handles redundant words used by agents.
items.note: No answer text is matched; agents submit code changes.

items.text: Handles negation modifiers used by agents.
items.note: No answer text is matched, so negation in answers does not arise.

items.text: Is robust against systematically listing all possible answers.
items.note: The answer is a code change graded by tests; listing all possible answers does not arise.

items.text: Ground truth is sufficiently complex to prevent guessing.
items.note: The answer is a code change, not a value that can be guessed.

items.text: Demonstrates documented or experimental evidence of the judge's accuracy, self-consistency, and agreement with human.
items.note: SWE-bench Verified uses no LLM judge.

items.text: Is designed to resist adversarial inputs and reward hacking.
items.note: SWE-bench Verified uses no LLM judge.

items.text: Verifies test cases for correctness and quality (e.g., by human).
items.quote: screen each sample of the SWE-bench test set for appropriately scoped unit tests and well-specified issue descriptions

items.text: Measures quality of test cases using objective metrics (e.g., code coverage, cyclomatic complexity control).
items.note: No source read reports code coverage, complexity, or another objective test quality metric.

items.text: Addresses potential edge cases.
Ensures comprehensive coverage of all relevant input variations (e.g., data types, memory layouts, value ranges).
Generates inputs that the code under testing is sensitive to.
items.note: Tests are written by the original pull request; no source says whether inputs are chosen for sensitivity of the code.

items.text: Covers all possible branches of user workflows.
Exercises all relevant parts of the code being tested.
Prevents non-deterministic ("flaky") test results.
items.note: No source read reports repeated runs or flakiness checks for the hidden tests; the eligibility records ran each task once.

items.text: Ground truth includes all states achievable after success.
items.quote: 35.5% of the audited tasks have strict test cases that enforce specific implementation details

items.text: Checks relevant and irrelevant states for the challenge.
items.quote: If the PASS_TO_PASS tests pass, then the edit has not inadvertently broken unrelated sections of the codebase.

items.text: Ground truth is complex to prevent trivial state modifications.
items.note: Grading runs tests on behavior, not a comparison of final state; the item reads as state matching.

items.text: Designs quality metrics that prevent exploitation (e.g., achieving high scores by reward hacking)
Includes measures to prevent data contamination, such as a private, held-out test set, or a lively updated dataset.
items.quote: SWE-bench problems are sourced from open-source repositories many model providers use for training purposes.

items.text: Includes measures or plans to consistently update challenges over time to avoid overfitting.
items.quote: Evaluations based on static datasets are inherently limited, and SWE-bench is no exception.

items.text: Includes quantitative analysis to assess the impact of unavoidable flaws (e.g., noise of ground truth).
items.quote: at least 59.4% of the audited problems have flawed test cases that reject functionally correct submissions

items.text: Reports metrics about statistical significance, such as confidence intervals.
items.quote: We ran a single seed using closest-documented or default hyperparameters for each scaffold
